newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan Diesel sees higher 1997 local sales.
newsitem.headline: Nissan Diesel sees higher 1997 local sales.

text.p: Nissan Diesel Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday it expects its domestic vehicle sales -- heavy trucks, light trucks and buses -- in calendar 1997 to rise 1.4 percent from the previous year to 32,400 vehciles, after a 9.2 percent fall in 1996.
Nissan Diesel, owned 39.8 percent by Nissan Motor Co Ltd, also estimated it would export 21,500 trucks and buses in 1997, up 0.5 percent from the previous year, after a 4.4 percent decline in 1996.
The company also estimated its domestic production of heavy trucks, light trucks and buses in 1997 at 49,600 vehicles, up 0.7 percent from 1996, when it had a 10.9 percent decline.
The size and other specifics of the truck were not immediately available.

Output of the Asia Truck is expected to reach 4,000 units this year, rising to 9,000 in 1998 and 12,000 in 1999. It aims to capture 25 percent of the market share of Japanese trucks in Asia by 1999, he said.
On the yen/dollar exchange rate, Saito said: "It would be best if the current level continues."
Nissan Diesel can conduct its business without difficulties if the yen's rate is 115-120 yen against the dollar, he said.

"If the current level of the yen/dollar rate continues, we don't need to plan additional drastic cost-cutting steps," he said. Nissan Diesel has been taking measures to cut costs to tackle sharp price falls.
